name: TLC5971RGER
title: TLC5971: RGB LED driver, 12 sink channels of 60 mA, 16-bit ES-PWM grayscale, on-chip 3.3 V regulator
summary: A twelve-output constant-current sink driver for RGB LEDs, arranged as four red, four green and four blue channels of up to 60 mA each. Every channel has a 16-bit grayscale PWM value and every color group a 7-bit current scale, all loaded over a two-wire data and clock link that chains from chip to chip with no latch line. One resistor sets full-scale current; a built-in 3.3 V regulator lets it run from 6 V to 17 V, or it runs directly from 3 V to 5.5 V. Comes in 20-pin HTSSOP (PWP) and 24-pin VQFN (RGE).
key_figures: 60 mA max per channel (recommended); 75 mA absolute
6 V to 17 V with internal regulator; 3 V to 5.5 V with VREG tied to VCC

The VQFN marking is TLC on one line and 5971 on the next.

circuits.title: Typical application, internal linear regulator, VCC = 6 V to 17 V
circuits.description: Two drivers in a chain run from one 6 V to 17 V supply. Each chip makes its own 3.3 V logic rail on VREG from VCC, held up by a 1 µF capacitor, and a resistor from IREF to ground fixes the full-scale sink current of all twelve outputs. The LED anodes go to VCC and each cathode to one output; a second LED per string is drawn as optional, since how many LEDs fit in series depends on VCC. The controller clocks data into SDTI and SCKI of the first chip, and SDTO and SCKO of each chip feed the next.

operation.text: Twelve constant-current sinks in three color groups of four (red, green, blue). Each output has a 16-bit PWM grayscale value; each group has a 7-bit brightness value that scales the current. One resistor on IREF sets the full-scale current, up to 60 mA. The PWM clock is either the internal oscillator or SCKI. A 3.3 V linear regulator lets the part run from 6 V to 17 V; with VREG tied to VCC it runs from 3 V to 5.5 V. Outputs can be paralleled for more current.

Data enters on SDTI and is clocked on rising SCKI edges into a 224-bit shift register, LSB first in and toward the MSB; the MSB drives SDTO, and SCKO repeats SCKI retimed to SDTO, so devices chain without limit. The top six bits are a write command. The register has no reset value at power-up. Data rate is up to 20 MHz.

When the internal latch pulse comes and the top six bits of the shift register equal 25h (100101b), the other 218 bits move into the 218-bit data latch: 192 bits of GS data, 21 bits of BC data and 5 function-control bits. With any other command the latch keeps its old contents.

There is no latch pin. The latch pulse is made internally once SCKI has stayed without a rising edge for eight times the interval between the last two rising edges. The wait therefore follows the clock rate, between 8 internal oscillator periods (666 ns) and 16384 periods (2.74 ms). The next SCKI edge must wait at least 8 internal clock periods (1.34 µs) after the latch pulse.

At power-up only BLANK is defined: it is 1, so all outputs are off. The shift register and the rest of the latch hold random data, so GS, BC and function data must be written before BLANK is cleared to 0.
Operation is released when VREG rises above 2.7 V typical (2.5 V to 2.9 V), with 400 mV typical hysteresis.

IOLCMax for every output is set by RIREF from IREF to GND (Equation 6, Table 1, Figure 5): 0.82 kΩ gives about 60 mA, 24.8 kΩ about 2 mA. To go below 2 mA, set IOLCMax at 2 mA or more and reduce it with BC. Tying IREF to GND forces all outputs off.
Each color group has a 7-bit BC value (BCR, BCG, BCB) that sets its current from 0 % to 100 % of IOLCMax in 128 steps (Equation 7, Table 2). A new BC value changes the current at once.

Each output has a 16-bit GS value giving 65536 steps of on-time. A 16-bit GS counter, clocked by the selected GS clock on the edge chosen by OUTTMG, times all outputs; on-time is the GS clock period times GS value (Equation 8). While BLANK = 1 the counter is held at 0 and the outputs are off, whatever the GS clock does.
The 65536-clock display period is cut into 128 segments of up to 512 GS clocks each, and an output's on-time is spread over the segments in a fixed bit-reversed order (Table 4, Figure 27).

DSPRPT (bit 214) = 1 makes the display period run again and again for as long as the GS clock runs, without touching BLANK. With DSPRPT = 0 one display period runs after BLANK goes to 0, or after a latch pulse when TMGRST = 1, and the outputs then stay off.

TMGRST (bit 215) = 1 makes every internal latch pulse clear the GS counter and turn the outputs off, as a BLANK toggle would; PWM restarts on the next GS clock edge, so the controller need not toggle BLANK. With TMGRST = 0 a latch pulse does not disturb the PWM.
OUTTMG (bit 217) picks the GS clock edge on which outputs switch: 1 for rising, 0 for falling. Giving alternate devices in a system opposite settings staggers their switching and lowers EMI.

To avoid a large current step when all twelve outputs turn on together, the red group switches first, then green, then blue, each group with a typical delay set by tD3, tD4 and tD5 (25, 50 and 75 ns typical).
Above TTSD (165 °C typical) all outputs are turned off. Once the junction cools below TTSD – THYS, output control resumes from the first GS clock of the next display period.

With VCC from 6 V to 17 V the internal regulator makes 3.3 V (3.1 V to 3.5 V) on VREG for up to 25 mA, with a 1 µF capacitor. The rail can feed external parts, and VREG pins of several devices may be joined for more current. For a 3 V to 5.5 V supply, VREG is tied to VCC.

With N devices chained, the controller shifts N × 224 bits, packet for the last device first, then waits for the latch pulse, which loads every device at once. The chain length has no limit as long as VCC is adequate at each device. Changing any one packet means sending the whole chain again.

For lighting that changes slowly. After power-up (outputs off), send N packets of 224 bits MSB first with command 25h, EXTGCK = 0, DSPRPT = 1 and BLANK = 0, back to back, then hold SCKI high or low for 8 times the last clock interval. All devices latch together and PWM starts or updates.

For video, or where all devices must run in step. Send N packets with EXTGCK = 1, DSPRPT = 0, TMGRST = 1 and BLANK = 0, then pause for the latch pulse. At least 1.34 µs later, clock SCKI with SDTI low: the first edge starts PWM and 65536 edges make one display period. Repeat for each frame.

operation.topic: Long chains in external clock mode
operation.text: For 256 devices (57344 bits per frame) the shift clock can double as GS clock: after the first latch, send 8192 SCKI clocks with SDTI low, then shift the next frame's 57344 bits, which completes the 65536-clock display period; then pause for the latch and repeat.

Decouple VCC with a 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor close to the VCC pin and ground plane. Spread several electrolytic capacitors over the board on VLED, depending on panel size; ripple on VLED should stay below 5 % of nominal.

Put the decoupling capacitor near VCC and ground; make ground copper as wide as possible for the large ground currents; keep the data and clock wires between chained devices short to limit inductance. Place RIREF close to the chip. Solder the exposed pad of either package to the board for heat and mechanical strength.
